role: CSV and plain-text RR parsing for RRDataImporter: separator/header/RR-column detection, per-row RR value choice, seconds->ms conversion, quoted-line splitting (used by Elite rows) and the shared date parser.
toplevel: dateFormatters is a lazily initialised static array built once on first parseDate call.

units.does: Splits into trimmed non-empty lines, detects separator and header from the first line, finds the RR column from the header, and returns RR values in ms from the data lines with empty metadata and a nil date.

branches.cond: there is at least one non-empty line
first line looks like a header
branches.effect: look up RR column index; otherwise nil (positional heuristics)
skip first line; otherwise parse it as data

flags.text: looksLikeHeader treats any first line containing 'ms', 'rr', 'time', 'ibi' or 'interval' as a header; a headerless file is fine, but a header with none of those words (e.g. 'beat,value') is parsed as data and silently dropped by the range filter, and a header naming e.g. 'timestamp_ms' only gets column 0 matched if no 'rr'/'ibi' column exists (rrColumnIndex only matches exact 'ms').

units.does: Filters out '#' and '//' comment lines, splits each by the separator, picks an RR value per row and keeps only values in 1...30000 ms.
Returns ';' when the first line contains ';' and no ',', else ','.
True when the lowercased first line contains rr, ibi, interval, time or ms.
Index of the first header column containing 'rr' or 'ibi', or equal to 'ms' or 'interval'; nil if none.

flags.text: A header column is chosen as RR when its name merely CONTAINS 'rr' or 'ibi', so a column such as 'current_hr', 'error' or 'correction' that precedes the real RR column is picked (firstIndex), and its values are trusted verbatim by rrValue with no physiological range check.

units.does: Chooses the RR value from a split row: the header-named column (unchecked), a single column (unchecked), else column 1 range-checked (300-2000), else column 0 range-checked only when column 1 did not parse.

branches.cond: rrColumnIndex is set AND the row has that many columns
branches.effect: use the header-named column; when the index is set but the row is shorter, fall through to the single/two-column heuristics below

branches.cond: header-column value parses as finite Double
branches.effect: convert and return with no physiological check; otherwise nil (row skipped)
return validRRValue(converted) (nil if outside 300-2000; column 0 is NOT tried)

units.does: Returns the value when HRVConstants.RRInterval.isValid (300-2000 ms), else nil.
Parses plain text: drops blank and comment lines, splits each line on whitespace/','/';', and keeps tokens that convert to valid 300-2000 ms RR values.
Token -> finite Double -> ms (seconds if <10) -> kept only if 300-2000 ms.
Splits a line on commas outside double quotes, removing quote characters and trimming each field.

branches.effect: emit current field; otherwise append char

units.does: Converts a value to Int ms: values < 10 are treated as seconds (x1000); non-finite -> 0; clamps to Int bounds; no range validation.

branches.effect: treated as seconds and multiplied by 1000 (this includes every negative value); otherwise taken as ms
return Int.min; otherwise Int(ms), truncating toward zero

flags.text: Seconds are converted with a truncating Int(value*1000), so binary floating point loses a millisecond on some exact inputs: e.g. 1.005, 1.001, 1.003 s become 1004/1000/1002 ms (12 values in 0.300-2.000 s). MillisecondOffset documents exactly this truncation as a defect and rounds instead.

units.does: Tries the six POSIX fixed formats in order, then ISO8601 with fractional seconds; nil if none match.

branches.effect: return date; after loop try ISO8601 (internet date time + fractional seconds only, so plain 'Z' strings without fraction rely on the first two fixed formats)

units.does: Builds the static list of DateFormatters for yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSSZ, yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ssZ, yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss, yyyy-MM-dd, MM/dd/yyyy HH:mm:ss, MM/dd/yyyy with the en_US_POSIX locale (whose Gregorian calendar the formatter adopts) and no explicit timeZone, so zone-less formats are read in the device's current time zone.
units.entry: static lazy initializer, run on first access from parseDate
